discovery: Dynamical mean-field theory of strongly correlated electron systems

nominees.name: Antoine Georges
nominees.affiliation: Collège de France, Paris; Flatiron Institute, New York; University of Geneva

motivation: Vollhardt (with Metzner) showed that lattice fermion models become locally exact in infinite dimensions. Georges and Kotliar then mapped the lattice problem onto a quantum impurity model solved self-consistently: dynamical mean-field theory. This provided the first non-perturbative, controlled description of the Mott metal-insulator transition, explaining how coherent quasiparticles and Hubbard bands coexist and how a correlated metal is destroyed. Combined with density-functional theory, DMFT became a quantitative, predictive framework for real materials: transition-metal oxides, actinides such as plutonium, iron pnictides, Hund's metals, cuprates and nickelates, with spectra and phase diagrams verified by photoemission and optical experiments. Its cluster and diagrammatic extensions and impurity solvers now define a worldwide computational field. DMFT fundamentally changed how physicists understand and compute quantum materials where electron interactions dominate, solving a central part of the many-electron problem that conventional band theory could not.
